title: Refusal Scope Envelope
purpose: Preserve an explicit learner refusal as a scoped, object-specific authority boundary without generalizing it into a task, purpose, person, or enduring preference.
rules: A refusal boundary must originate in explicit learner-authored human evidence.
The persisted refused object must match the exact source object and scope.
A refusal of wording or a nudge does not silently become refusal of its parent task or purpose.
A different object remains available for collaboration unless separately refused.
Resuming the exact refused object requires a later explicit learner request.
Silence, partial uptake, or ambiguity may not be promoted into generalized disengagement.
Persistence may not create a person profile, derived preference, copied raw dialogue, broader collection, or production self-modification.
Human, synthetic, system, and scholarly evidence remain distinct.
